summary: Iteration 4 verified the post-iteration-3 fixes. Backend: 50/50 pass (38 in test_custom_auth.py plus 12 new in test_iteration4_lockout.py). The new login_failures lockout works: 5 failures from one IP+email give 429 on the 6th, 10 failures from rotating X-Forwarded-For IPs give 429 for that email, email case is normalised, and a successful login clears only that IP's failures. Regression of admin login, /auth/me, logout and staff 403 on admin-only routes passed. Frontend: a first-time visitor to /admin and a visitor reopening /admin after Log Out both reach /admin/login with no expired message (PASS). A reload after expiry goes to /admin/login with no message, which the brief allows. All 5 admin pages load. One bug: when the session expires and the user clicks a sidebar link (e.g. Enquiries), they are redirected to /admin/login WITHOUT the 'Your session has expired' message. The message only shows when a 401 comes back while the user stays on a page (e.g. typing in the Enquiries search box).

minor.issue: Per-email lock (10 in 15 min from any IP) lets an attacker lock the real admin out on purpose. This is a known trade-off and acceptable, but there is no admin unlock path other than editing the DB.

ui_bugs.issue: The expired message is lost when an expired session is detected through sidebar navigation. RCA: in react-router-dom 7.18.4 declarative mode, the function returned by useNavigate() changes on every pathname change. AdminShell's effect therefore re-runs GET /auth/me on every admin navigation (seen in the network log: /auth/me is called after each NAV). On expiry, that /auth/me 401 arrives first (the Enquiries call is debounced by 250ms and the page unmounts), and Shell redirects with navigate('/admin/login', {replace:true}) with no {expired:true}. Repro: log in, set the session's expires_at to the past, click admin-nav-enquiries, and the login page shows no admin-login-error. Fix options: (a) run the /auth/me effect once (store navigate in a ref, deps []) so in-page useAdminApi calls handle the 401, or (b) in Shell's catch, pass state:{expired:true} when member was already loaded (a functional setMember / ref check) so first-time visitors still get no message.

On an in-page 401, the user sees the inline expired message AND a sonner toast with the same text, because each page's .catch(toast.error(errMsg(e))) also fires. Suppress the toast for 401 (e.g. useAdminApi rethrows a marked error, or pages skip the toast when status===401).

action_items: Keep the 'session expired' message when expiry is found through sidebar navigation. Either run AdminShell's /auth/me check only once on mount (navigate in a ref, deps []), or pass state {expired:true} when a re-check returns 401 after member was already loaded.
Optional: also consider that AdminShell re-fetching /auth/me on every nav (and useAdminApi's `call` identity changing per nav, which re-triggers page loads) is extra network traffic.
Optional: suppress the duplicate toast on 401 in admin pages.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminShell.jsx: useEffect deps [navigate] are not stable in react-router v7 declarative mode, so the effect re-runs on every route change. This is the root cause of the lost expired message.
common.js useAdminApi: useCallback([navigate]) also changes identity on every nav. Pages whose load callbacks depend on `call` refetch for that reason.

server.py login: the two count_documents calls and the insert are not atomic, so a burst of parallel requests can go slightly over 5/10. Low risk and acceptable; the TTL index (1h) on login_failures.at keeps the collection small.

Previous test suite issue (fixed in tests): test_custom_auth.py wrote failed logins for the REAL admin email (test_wrong_password, test_lockout_429) and cleaned the obsolete login_attempts collection. With the new per-email lock of 10, running the suite a few times within 15 min could lock out the real admin.

context_for_next_testing_agent: To test UI expiry without pymongo in the browser env: create a TEST_ staff user via API, run a background python watcher that sets expires_at to the past for that user's sessions about 5s after created_at, log in as that staff user in Playwright, wait 8s, then click admin-nav-enquiries (nav path, currently FAILS) or type in admin-enquiry-search-input (in-page path, PASSES). Run pytest with the configured xdist (do not pass -p no:xdist). Never use the admin email for lockout tests.
rca of the issue: The expired message is missing after a nav-triggered 401 because react-router 7's useNavigate identity changes per pathname. AdminShell's useEffect([navigate]) then re-calls /auth/me on each navigation, and its 401 branch redirects without state.expired. That beats the page's own useAdminApi call, which would have set expired:true. Reproduced 2/2 in the browser; the in-page 401 path works (message shown).
